recipes.title: Roasted Salmon & Veg Traybake
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here. Lemon and garlic don't halve cleanly — use a whole lemon and a small pinch of garlic to taste.
method: Preheat the oven to 200ºC/400ºF/gas 6.
Cook the potatoes in boiling salted water for 10-12 minutes until cooked through, adding the green beans for the final 2 minutes. Drain.
Tip the veg into a bowl, halve and add the tomatoes, destone and add the olives along with half the basil leaves. Add a little olive oil, toss and tip into a roasting tray.

Toss the salmon fillets with a little olive oil and a squeeze of lemon juice, season lightly. Lay on top of the vegetables skin-side up, top with a couple of lemon slices, and roast for 10 minutes until cooked through.

For the yoghurt: bash the remaining basil with a pinch of salt, add the garlic and bash again. Mix in the mustard, Greek yoghurt and remaining lemon juice, plus a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil. Season to taste and serve with the salmon traybake.

recipes.title: Summer Lamb and Orzo Salad
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here.

ingredients.item: red chilli, deseeded and finely chopped (optional — mild background warmth only)
Handful finely chopped fresh mint, plus extra to garnish
preserved lemon, deseeded and finely chopped
pine nuts, toasted in a dry pan for 2 minutes

method: Cook the orzo in boiling water for 8-10 minutes until just tender, adding the peas for the last 2-3 minutes. Drain, refresh under cold water and drain again. Tip into a bowl and mix in the feta, courgette ribbons, chilli and chopped mint.
Whisk the preserved lemon, lemon juice, 1 tbsp of the olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Pour over the orzo, stir and transfer to a serving dish.
Heat a griddle to high. Rub the remaining olive oil over the lamb, season both sides. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until charred and tender.
Arrange lamb over the orzo. Scatter over the pine nuts and extra mint. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Lemony Courgette Linguine
method: Cook the linguine in boiling salted water according to packet instructions. Drain, reserving a mugful of cooking water.
Slice the courgettes lengthways, then into long matchsticks (or use the julienne cutter on a mandolin).
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the courgettes and cook for 4 minutes, tossing regularly. Finely slice the mint leaves and stir in.
Toss the drained pasta into the pan with a splash of reserved cooking water. Finely grate in most of the Parmesan and a little lemon zest, squeeze in all the juice. Toss well, taste and season.
Dish up, grate over the remaining Parmesan and drizzle with 1 tsp extra virgin olive oil.

recipes.title: Quick Sticky Chicken Salad
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here.

ingredients.item: Zest of 1/2 lemon and juice of 3/4 lemon
Small bunch fresh mint, half chopped, half kept whole
skinless chicken breasts, each sliced into 3 pieces
garlic ciabatta, sliced in half lengthways
tinned chickpeas, drained and rinsed (half a 400g tin)

method: Mix together the lemon zest and juice (keeping about 1 tbsp juice back for the dressing), honey, 1 tbsp of the oil and the chopped mint. Season and add the chicken, stir to coat, leave 10 minutes.
Blanch the broad beans in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain, refresh in cold water, drain again and slip from their skins. Tear the ciabatta into pieces and grill for 5 minutes until golden.
Heat a griddle over high heat. Cook chicken 2-3 minutes each side until charred, sticky and cooked through.

Toss the lettuce, broad beans, ciabatta, chickpeas, tomatoes, cucumber, parsley and remaining mint in a large bowl. Whisk the remaining oil, 1 tbsp lemon juice and mustard into a dressing. Season, pour over, add the warm chicken and toss.

recipes.title: Mediterranean Halloumi Salad

ingredients.item: roasted red and yellow peppers in oil, drained and sliced

method: Place the onion in a small bowl, cover with freshly boiled water, leave a minute, then drain and rinse in cold water. Lay the sliced tomatoes on a platter, scatter over the blanched onion, roasted peppers, caperberries and olives. Drizzle with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, season well, and set aside.

Thickly slice the halloumi. Heat a frying pan over high heat and cook the cheese in batches for a minute on each side until golden. Add to the platter, drizzle with the remaining olive oil, scatter over basil leaves, and serve with crusty bread.

recipes.title: Creamy Garlic Prawn Pasta

ingredients.item: mascarpone, crème fraîche or double cream
raw king prawns, defrosted if frozen
chopped soft herbs (chives, parsley or tarragon, or a mix)

method: Cook the linguine following pack instructions.
Meanwhile, heat the butter and oil in a large frying pan over low heat and cook the garlic and chilli flakes (if using) for 2 minutes until fragrant.

Pour in the wine and simmer a few minutes until reduced by half, then stir in the mascarpone and season well. Add the prawns and cook until pink and cooked through. Stir in the herbs, then tip in the drained linguine and toss with a splash of the cooking water until saucy and slippery. Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and serve.

recipes.title: Slow-Roasted Shoulder of Spring Lamb
recipes.note: Mostly hands-off. In by 2pm, on the table at 7pm with almost no intervention.

ingredients.item: lamb bones and trimmings (ask your butcher)

method: Marinate (1–2 hrs before) — Score the lamb skin lightly. Rub all over with the salt, pepper, chopped rosemary, sage and olive oil. Leave at room temperature for at least 1–2 hours.

Colour the bones (230°C / Gas 8) — Heat the rapeseed oil in a large heavy roasting pan over medium heat. Add the bones and trimmings and colour for 7–10 minutes until lightly golden. Add the garlic, brown for 3 minutes, then remove the pan from the heat.

Start the roast — Sit the lamb shoulder on top of the bones. Roast at 230°C for 20 minutes. Meanwhile, bring the wine to a boil in a small pan, let it bubble for 30 seconds, then add 400ml hot water, the bay leaf and thyme.

Long, slow cook (150°C / Gas 2, 4 hours) — Take the lamb out, baste with pan juices, skim excess fat, and pour the wine-water mixture into the pan. Cover loosely with foil. Return to the oven at 150°C and roast for a further 4 hours, basting every 30 minutes. Add another 100ml water if juices reduce too far.
Rest and finish — Remove the lamb and rest. Strain the juices into a small saucepan, skim the fat, reheat until bubbling, and season. The meat will be fall-apart tender — serve at the table.
notes: Serve with a gratin dauphinois, celeriac gratin, or braised seasonal vegetables. Crushed New Potatoes and Griddled Courgettes both pair with this.

Why it works with premier cru Burgundy: slow-cooked lamb shoulder has enough richness to stand up to the wine without overpowering it. The rosemary, sage and thyme echo the earthiness and forest floor notes in the Pinot, while the clean wine-and-water jus keeps things elegant.

recipes.title: Pan-Roasted Pork Tenderloin with Fennel
method: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F.
Pat the pork dry with paper towel. Rub ground fennel seeds all over the meat, season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the tenderloin on all sides, about 6 minutes. Remove and set aside on a plate.
Cut fennel bulbs into 1.5cm wedges. Using the same pan, sauté fennel and garlic over medium heat until fennel is golden and tender, about 6 minutes.
Add wine and deglaze the pan, scraping up any brown bits. Add butter and broth; stir to combine.
Place pork on top of the fennel and transfer the pan to the oven. Roast until the internal temperature reaches 63–65°C, about 15 minutes.
Transfer pork to a cutting board and rest for 10 minutes.
While pork rests, return the skillet to the stovetop and simmer the liquid until almost completely reduced.
Add lemon juice, reduce heat, and stir in the reserved chopped fennel fronds.
Slice pork, serve over fennel wedges, and spoon sauce over the top.
notes: Use an instant-read thermometer — 63°C keeps the pork juicy. Don't skip the rest.

recipes.title: Sea Bass Crudo
recipes.note: Serves 2 as a starter. No cooking required.

ingredients.item: sea bass fillets, skinned and pin-boned
Flaky sea salt and black pepper

method: Place the fish and your serving plates in the freezer for 10 minutes beforehand — cold fish slices more cleanly and stays fresher longer on the plate.
Using a sharp knife, slice the fish thinly on a 45° angle, about 2–3mm thick. Lay slices in a single layer on the cold plates.
Sprinkle with flaky salt, then drizzle lemon juice over the fish, followed by the olive oil.
Crack over black pepper and add any optional garnishes.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ask your fishmonger to skin and pin-bone the sea bass for you. Quality of fish is everything here — buy the freshest you can find.

recipes.title: Perfect Pan-Fried Chicken Breasts

ingredients.item: anchovy fillet, drained (or 1/2 tsp chopped capers)
Small handful parsley or chives, chopped

method: Put the chicken breasts in a large food bag and bash the thicker parts with a rolling pin until an even 1.5-1.7cm thick. Add the salt and massage into the chicken. Leave at room temperature to dry-brine for 30 minutes (no more).

Remove from the bag and brush off excess salt. Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat, add the oil. Once simmering, add the chicken. Cook 5-6 minutes each side without moving it, for a strong caramelised sear. In the final minute, add the butter and baste the chicken once it's foaming. Rest the chicken 5 minutes.

While resting, add the anchovy to the butter in the pan, stirring until dissolved. Add the vinegar, swirl and cook 1 minute. Slice the chicken against the grain, plate up, add resting juices to the sauce with the chopped herbs, and pour over the chicken.
notes: The original recipe suggests roast new potatoes and seasonal veg as sides — swap in boiled new potatoes or a simple summer salad to keep it fully oven-free in hot weather.

recipes.title: Authentic Greek Salad (Horiatiki)

source.name: The Mediterranean Dish / My Greek Dish / The Greek Foodie

recipes.note: Traditional village salad — no lettuce, no fuss.

ingredients.item: large ripe tomatoes, cut into chunky wedges
green bell pepper, sliced into rings
A generous handful of Kalamata olives
block of feta cheese (placed whole on top — do not crumble)
Extra virgin olive oil (good quality — this is the dressing)

method: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, green pepper, and red onion in a wide bowl or on a platter. Season lightly with salt.
Scatter over the olives.
Place the block of feta on top — do not crumble it.
Drizzle generously with extra virgin olive oil. Add a splash of red wine vinegar if using.
Finish with a pinch of dried oregano over the feta and a crack of black pepper.
Serve immediately, or let it sit for a few minutes so the tomato juices start to mingle with the oil.
notes: No lettuce. Ever. That's the westernised version.
No lemon juice — it doesn't belong in horiatiki.
The feta goes on as a whole block, not crumbled.
Cut everything chunky — this is a rustic village salad, not a finely chopped one.
The quality of your tomatoes and olive oil makes or breaks this dish. Use the ripest tomatoes you can find.

recipes.title: Lamb Cutlets in Basil Sauce

ingredients.item: Small handful fresh thyme, leaves picked
mushrooms, brushed clean and torn (wild, or chestnut/oyster)

method: Best cooked on a hot barbecue, or use a preheated ridged griddle/frying pan. Flatten the cutlets slightly. Bash the thyme with a little olive oil in a pestle and mortar, rub over the cutlets, and season both sides.

Cook the mushrooms dry on the hot pan, both sides, to mark them, then set aside in a large bowl. Cook the lamb: about 3-4 minutes each side for cutlets around 1.5cm thick, for medium (less time for rare).
Add the lamb to the mushroom bowl, drizzle with olive oil, tear over the parsley, squeeze over the lemon juice, season, and toss. Rest so the juices soak into the mushrooms.

Make the sauce: pound the pine nuts to a pulp in a pestle and mortar, transfer to a bowl. Pound the basil to a pulp and add to the pine nuts, loosening with olive oil until it drops easily off a spoon.
Balance with balsamic vinegar to taste for a good zing. Give the lamb and mushrooms a final toss. Serve on a platter with the sauce and a simple watercress salad on the side.

recipes.title: Lemon Thyme and Fennel Butterflied Leg of Lamb
recipes.time: 25-30 mins on the barbecue + 1-24 hrs marinating

ingredients.item: good-quality leg of lamb, butterflied (ask your butcher), trimmed of fat
Chunky chips (or a summer salad), to serve

method: Cut and open up any thicker areas of meat so it's all about 4-5cm thick. Mix all the other ingredients (apart from the chips) together in a large shallow dish, add the lamb and coat well. Cover and marinate at room temperature for 1 hour, or chill and marinate for up to 24 hours.
If using a charcoal barbecue, light about 30 minutes before you want to cook. For a gas barbecue, preheat 10 minutes beforehand.

Lift the lamb out of the dish, let excess oily marinade drain away, then lay on the barbecue. Cook over direct high heat for 25-30 minutes, turning occasionally and moving away from flare-ups, until well-coloured but pink and juicy in the middle (or 60°C on a meat thermometer). Cook longer if you prefer it more done.
Transfer to a board, cover and rest for 5 minutes. Carve into thick slices and serve.

recipes.title: Thai Basil Chicken (Pad Kra Pao Gai)
recipes.note: Hob only — no oven. Recipe as written serves 1; doubled here for 2. Andy prefers milder heat than the traditional version — start with 2-3 chillies rather than the 8 below, or deseed them.

ingredients.item: chicken breasts, cut into small bite-sized pieces (about 400g)
Thai chillies — start with 2-3 for less heat (see note)
Thai holy basil leaves (Thai sweet basil as a substitute)

method: Get a pot of jasmine rice on so it's ready when the chicken is.

Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a wok or frying pan over high heat. Fry the eggs one at a time, splashing hot oil over the yolk as it cooks, until crisp at the edges and the yolk is still runny. Drain and set aside.
Pound or finely chop the garlic and chillies together — just enough to bring out the oils, no need for a paste. Pluck the basil leaves from their stems.
Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in the wok over high heat. Add the garlic and chillies and stir-fry about 20 seconds until fragrant, without burning.
Add the chicken and stir-fry continuously until just cooked through, 2-3 minutes. Add a splash of water if the pan looks dry.
Add the oyster sauce, light soy sauce, sugar and dark soy sauce. Stir-fry another 30 seconds.
Add the basil, fold it through, and take off the heat immediately — it only needs a few seconds to wilt.
Serve over the rice with a fried egg on the side.
notes: Holy basil (bai kra prao) has a peppery flavour and is the authentic choice. Thai sweet basil works as a substitute but loses that peppery note.
Pairs well with an off-dry Riesling — the fruit and acidity balance the chilli heat and salty sauce.

recipes.title: Roast Turbot with Leeks, Tarragon and Riesling
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 3-4 off a 1.2-1.5kg turbot; halved here for 2 — pairs with Rockfish's Whole Turbot for Two (600g). Leeks and lemon don't halve perfectly cleanly — rounded up to 2 leeks and half a lemon's juice.

ingredients.item: leeks, outer leaves removed and washed

method: Heat the oven to 180°C fan/gas 6. Finely slice the spring onions and fennel, then cut the leeks into 3cm chunks. Melt the butter in a large flameproof roasting dish over medium heat, add the veg, season well with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened (8-10 minutes).

Pour in the Riesling, stir through, then turn off the heat. Lay the turbot on top of the vegetables, white skin side down, and make 2 slashes across its back. Season with a pinch of salt and roast for 15-18 minutes — it's ready when a milky liquid appears in the slashes.

Scatter over the tarragon leaves and squeeze over the lemon juice. Bring the dish to the table and carve — there are 4 fillets on a turbot: lift the first 2 off the top, then flip and remove the 2 underneath.
notes: Wine pairing: an oaked white Rioja or a mature white Burgundy — enough depth and structure for the rich, buttery sauce. (Matching Food & Wine)

recipes.title: Beef & Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here. Ginger, chilli and lime don't halve perfectly cleanly — use a smaller piece of ginger, half a chilli, and half a lime to taste.

ingredients.item: Egg noodles or steamed rice, to serve

method: Blanch the broccoli in boiling salted water for 10 minutes; drain.
Finely slice the onion and garlic, chop the ginger, slice the chilli, and cut the lime into wedges.
Pound the coriander seeds with salt and pepper using a pestle and mortar.
Slice the steak into finger-sized strips and coat with the spice mixture.
Heat a wok on high heat; add a little olive oil, then cook the onion, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the beef and fry for 2 minutes. Add the broccoli and fry for a further 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in the soy sauce and sesame oil; toss to coat.
Serve with egg noodles or steamed rice, topped with the remaining chilli and a squeeze of lime juice.

recipes.title: Mushroom Stroganoff

ingredients.item: mixed mushrooms (e.g. portabellini and woodland), sliced/torn
curly parsley, finely chopped (half a 25g pack)
cooked long grain rice, to serve

method: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over low-medium heat. Add the onion and garlic and cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add the mushrooms, increase the heat to medium-high, and stir-fry for 5 minutes until they release their moisture. Add the brandy, if using, and cook until evaporated.
Stir in the paprika and miso, pour in the stock, and simmer for 2 minutes to reduce. Remove from the heat and stir in the soured cream and most of the parsley.
Cook the rice according to pack instructions. Serve the stroganoff over the rice, garnished with the reserved parsley and a pinch of paprika.

recipes.title: Pan-Fried Cod with Prawn & Lemon Butter
recipes.note: Recipe as written serves 4; halved here.

ingredients.item: lemon, finely grated rind and juice
spinach leaves, lightly steamed, to serve

method: Coat the cod with the seasoned flour. Heat the oil and half the butter in a large frying pan until foaming. Add the cod and fry for 4 minutes per side until cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Wipe the pan clean. Add the remaining butter and heat until melted. Add the prawns and lemon rind, warming gently for 20-30 seconds, then stir in the lemon juice.
Serve the cod with the steamed spinach and pour over the lemon-prawn butter. Season with freshly ground black pepper.
notes: Can be made with another white fish, such as haddock, if you prefer.
